stops: At every $r > 0$ the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, $g_{rr} = 1/(1 + r^2/L^2) < 1$, so no surface of revolution in flat space carries the equator of a slice of constant $t$. It is the hyperbolic plane of curvature $-1/L^2$: a piece of it lies in flat space on Eugenio Beltrami's pseudosphere, and David Hilbert proved in 1901 that no surface in flat space carries the whole of it.
